traps.item: The output does not present the open-data death counts as the official NYC toll (reporting them as counts in this dataset is fine).
traps.note: open-data deaths differ from official counts (2025: 229 here vs 205 NYC DOT)

traps.item: The output makes no causal attribution (e.g. 'because of the pandemic') that the data cannot support.

ped_killed_by_year.query: SELECT year(crash_date) k, sum(number_of_pedestrians_killed) pedestrians_killed FROM '<parquet>' WHERE year(crash_date) BETWEEN 2013 AND 2025 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

traps.item: If counts are pooled over 2013–2025, the output says that pre-2020 years dominate or that crash reporting changed in 2020.

If per-day averages or 'X% fewer on <day>' comparisons are given, the arithmetic is right (e.g. Sunday has 24% fewer than the mean weekday, Friday 32% more) and unequal day counts (678/679) are handled or noted.
traps.note: Tue and Wed occur 679 times, other days 678

crashes_by_weekday.query: SELECT dayofweek(crash_date) k, count(*) crashes FROM '<parquet>' WHERE year(crash_date) BETWEEN 2013 AND 2025 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

traps.item: Claims about cyclist deaths changing sharply (e.g. 'tripled') are qualified by the small counts (10 → 31).
The output does not claim that motorist + cyclist deaths are all deaths (pedestrians and unclassified deaths exist).
traps.note: residual 6–20 deaths per year outside the three mode columns, 2021–2025

motorist_cyclist_killed_by_year.query: SELECT year(crash_date) k, sum(number_of_motorist_killed) motorist_killed, sum(number_of_cyclist_killed) cyclist_killed FROM '<parquet>' WHERE year(crash_date) BETWEEN 2013 AND 2025 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

traps.item: If a borough filter (borough = 'BROOKLYN') is used, the output discloses that crashes with no borough recorded (19.9–38.1% per year) are excluded.
The output does not call Brooklyn 'safer' or 'less safe' from counts alone without saying that there is no pedestrian exposure measure.
If a per-crash rate spanning 2020 is shown, the output caveats the 2020 change in crash recording.
Claims about pedestrian deaths changing are qualified by the small counts (about 30–39 per year).

brooklyn_ped_injured_killed_by_year.query: SELECT year(crash_date) k, sum(number_of_pedestrians_injured) pedestrians_injured, sum(number_of_pedestrians_killed) pedestrians_killed FROM '<parquet>' WHERE year(crash_date) BETWEEN 2013 AND 2025 AND upper(borough)='BROOKLYN' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

brooklyn_crashes_by_year.query: SELECT year(crash_date) k, count(*) crashes FROM '<parquet>' WHERE year(crash_date) BETWEEN 2013 AND 2025 AND upper(borough)='BROOKLYN' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

traps.item: Severity per crash (deaths or injuries per crash) is described as such, not as the risk of being on the street at night (no traffic volume by hour exists).

NA if the option uses no killed or injured counts. Otherwise the analysis window excludes 2026, or 2026 rows (killed count NULL in 87.8% of May-2026 and 100% of June-2026 rows) are excluded or handled, and sums are NULL-safe.
traps.note: a window including 2026 biases fatality rates low
the cut is one of several defensible ones

day_night_06_17.query: SELECT CASE WHEN hour(crash_time) BETWEEN 6 AND 17 THEN 'day' ELSE 'night' END k, count(*) crashes, sum(number_of_persons_killed) killed, sum(number_of_persons_injured) injured FROM '<parquet>' WHERE year(crash_date) BETWEEN 2013 AND 2025 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

by_hour.query: SELECT hour(crash_time) k, count(*) crashes, sum(number_of_persons_killed) killed, sum(number_of_persons_injured) injured FROM '<parquet>' WHERE year(crash_date) BETWEEN 2013 AND 2025 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

I1.required_statement: Per-mile (per vehicle-mile) risk cannot be determined from this data because it has no vehicle-miles or traffic volume.

traps.item: If a per-reported-crash rate spanning 2020 is shown, the output caveats the 2020 change in crash recording (fewer minor crashes reported).
A per-reported-crash rate, if shown, is not presented as a substitute for per-mile risk.
No vehicle-miles figure is imported, assumed or estimated from outside the data.
